text: Fazal Elahi Chaudhry (1 January 1904 – 2 June 1982) was a Pakistani barrister, politician, and statesman who served as the fifth president of Pakistan from 1973 until his resignation in September 1978, following the 1977 coup d'état that overthrew Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's government and established martial law under Zia-ul-Haq. He was the first legislatively-elected president in Pakistan's history and served as a constitutional figurehead under the 1973 constitution, which shifted executive power to the prime minister. Born in Marala, Kharian Tehsil of Gujrat District, Punjab, into an influential Punjabi Muslim Gujjar family, Chaudhry received his early education in Kharian, then attended Aligarh Muslim University in 1920, earning his LLB in civil law in 1924. He later returned to Punjab, studied at the University of the Punjab, obtaining a master's degree in political science in 1925 and an advanced LLM in Law and Justice in 1927. After establishing a law firm in Lahore, he began practising civil law and returned to Gujrat. In 1930, he was elected unopposed to the Gujrat District Board. He joined the All-India Muslim League in 1942, became president of the Punjab Muslim League for Gujrat District in 1945, and participated in the 1946 Indian provincial elections on the Muslim League ticket. After Pakistan's independence in 1947, he was appointed parliamentary secretary and later served as education and health minister in Liaquat Ali Khan's cabinet. He represented Pakistan at the United Nations in 1952 and was elected to the West Punjab Assembly in 1951. In 1956, he was elected to the West Pakistan Assembly and served as its first Speaker from 20 May 1956 to 7 October 1958. He joined the Convention Muslim League and was elected deputy speaker of the National Assembly in 1965, serving until 1969 when Yahya Khan declared martial law. In 1970, he was elected to the National Assembly on the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) ticket and later became its speaker in 1972. Under the 1973 constitution, Chaudhry contested the presidential election against Khan Amirzadah Khan of the National Awami Party (Wali), winning with an absolute electoral college majority of 139 votes to Khan's 45, and was sworn in on 14 August 1973, becoming the first ethnic Punjabi president. He succeeded Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who became prime minister. As a figurehead, the presidency had become ceremonial, with executive authority vested in the prime minister. After the 1977 coup d'état, Bhutto's government and all provincial governments were overthrown by Zia-ul-Haq, who assumed the role of chief martial law administrator; Chaudhry continued as president but had no influence over governmental, military, or national affairs. Due to contentious relations with the Zia-led military regime, he resigned on 16 September 1978, handing over the presidency to Zia-ul-Haq. Chaudhry remained a respected legislator and politician throughout his career and died of a heart ailment on 2 June 1982 in Lahore at the age of 78.
